'''Nediljko '''"'''Ned'''"''' Budisa''' ({{langx|hr|Nediljko Budiša}}; born 21 November 1966) is a Croatian biochemist, professor and holder of the Tier 1 [[Canada Research Chair]] (CRC) for chemical [[synthetic biology]] at the [[University of Manitoba]]. He contributed to the fields of [[genetic code]] engineering, chemical synthetic biology and [[Xenobiology]]. Of [[interdisciplinarity|interdisciplinary]] nature, his scientific contributions relate to [[bioorganic chemistry|bioorganic]], [[medical chemistry]], [[structural biology]], and [[biophysics]]. He is the author of a textbook in his research field: "Engineering the genetic code: expanding the amino acid repertoire for the design of novel proteins".<ref>{{cite book
| title = The book at the Wiley Online Library
| doi = 10.1002/3527607188
| isbn = 978-3-527-31243-6
|year = 2005|last1 = Budisa|first1 = Nediljko}}</ref>

==Early life, education and career==

Ned Budisa earned a high school teacher diploma in Chemistry and Biology in 1990, a B.S. in [[Molecular Biology]] and MSc in [[Biophysics]] in 1993 from the [[University of Zagreb]]. He received a PhD in 1997 from the [[Technical University of Munich]] where his thesis advisor was Professor [[Robert Huber]]. He also [[Habilitation|habilitated]] at the Technical University of Munich in 2005 and worked afterwards as a junior group leader ("Molecular Biotechnology")<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.biochem.mpg.de/en/rg/budisa/
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070610062730/http://www.biochem.mpg.de/en/rg/budisa/
| archive-date = 2007-06-10
| title = Molecular Biotechnology
| publisher = Max Planck Institute
| access-date = 2017-08-10
}}</ref> at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry]] in Munich. Between 2007 and 2010 he was a member of CIPS<sup>M</sup> in Munich.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.cipsm.de/cipsm-professorships/
| title = List of CIPS<sup>M</sup> professors
| access-date = 2017-08-10
}}</ref> He was appointed as full professor of [[biocatalysis]] at the TU Berlin in 2010<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.biocat.tu-berlin.de/menue/biokatalyse/parameter/en/
| title = Website of the Biocatalysis group
| access-date = 2017-08-10
| archive-date = April 16, 2020
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200416050751/https://www.biocat.tu-berlin.de/menue/biokatalyse/parameter/en/
}}</ref> until the end of 2018, when he accepted the Tier 1 CRC position in Chemical [[Synthetic Biology]] at the [[University of Manitoba]].<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.sci.umanitoba.ca/chemistry/news-and-events/news/welcome-dr-ned-budisa
| title = University of Manitoba welcoming Ned Budisa
| work = Department of Chemistry
| access-date = 2019-08-17
| date = October 16, 2018
| last1 = Luong
| first1 = Horace
| archive-date = August 1, 2019
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190801055340/https://www.sci.umanitoba.ca/chemistry/news-and-events/news/welcome-dr-ned-budisa
}}</ref> He remained affiliated with TU Berlin through an [[adjunct professor]]ship (2018–2023) and was also a member of the Excellence Cluster 'Unifying Systems in Catalysis' (UniSysCat).<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://www.unisyscat.de | title = UniSysCat Cluster of Excellence
| access-date = 2019-08-17
}}</ref> In 2014, he founded the first Berlin [[International Genetically Engineered Machine|iGEM]] team.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://igem.biocat.tu-berlin.de
| title = iGEM team Berlin
| access-date = 2017-08-10
}}</ref> In 2022, he founded the first iGEM team at the University of Manitoba.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://news.umanitoba.ca/science-students-win-silver-at-international-biotech-competition/
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20260707194216/https://umtoday-wordpress.ad.umanitoba.ca/science-students-win-silver-at-international-biotech-competition/
| archive-date = 2026-07-07
| title = UM Today {{pipe}} Faculty of Science {{pipe}} Science students win silver at international biotech competition
| access-date = 2026-07-07
}}</ref>

==Research==

Ned Budisa works in [[Xenobiology#Genetic code engineering|genetic code engineering]] and [[Chemical biology|chemical synthetic biology]], developing ''[[in vivo]]'' techniques to introduce genetically encoded modifications into [[protein]]s and entire [[proteomes]]. He  applies the [[Expanded genetic code#Selective pressure incorporation .28SPI.29 method for production of alloproteins|Selective Pressure Incorporation (SPI) method]]<ref>{{cite journal
| last = Budisa | first = N.
| doi = 10.1002/anie.200300646
| year = 2004
| title = Prolegomena to future efforts on genetic code engineering by expanding its amino acid repertoire
| journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition
| volume = 43
| pages = 3387–3428
}}</ref> that enables single and multiple<ref>{{cite journal
| last1 = Lepthien | first1 = S.
| last2 = Merkel | first2 = L.
| last3 = Budisa | first3 = N.
| doi = 10.1002/anie.201000439
| pmid = 20575122
| year = 2010
| title = In Vivo Double and Triple Labeling of Proteins Using Synthetic Amino Acids
| journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition
| volume = 49
| issue = 32
| pages = 5446–5450
}}</ref> in vivo incorporations of synthetic (i.e. non-canonical) amino acid analogs in proteins, preferably by sense [[codon reassignment]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1 = Bohlke | first1 = N.
| last2 = Budisa | first2 = N.
| doi = 10.1111/1574-6968.12371
| year = 2014

| journal = FEMS Microbiology Letters

| pmc = 4237120
| pmid = 24433543
| s2cid = 5735708
}}</ref> His methodology allows for fine chemical manipulations of a few amino acid side chains, mainly of [[proline]], [[tryptophan]] and [[methionine]]. These experiments are often assisted with metabolic engineering techniques in collaboration with Prof. Sven Panke.<ref>{{cite journal

| pmid = 28671771

| year = 2021
| title = Multiomics Analysis Provides Insight into the Laboratory Evolution of Escherichia coli toward the Metabolic Usage of Fluorinated Indoles
| doi = 10.1021/acscentsci.0c00679
| doi-access = free| journal = ACS Central Science
| volume = 7
| issue = 1
| pages = 81–92
| pmc = 7844855
}}</ref> as [[xenobiotic]] compounds (in collaboration with Beate Koksch from the [[Free University of Berlin]]) has led to the discovery of exceptional physiological plasticity in microbial cultures during [[adaptation|adaptive]] laboratory [[evolution]], making them potential environmentally friendly tools for new [[bioremediation]] strategies.

Ned Budisa is also actively involved in the debate of possible societal, ethical and philosophical impacts of radical genetic code engineering in the context of [[artificial cell|synthetic cells]] and [[life]] as well as technologies derived thereof.<ref>{{cite book
